messages:
maria (Support): heads-up — customer jordan reports spikes of 502/504s hitting our hosted inference endpoint starting ~2025-11-02T14:12Z. they see TLS handshake timeouts and gateway failures. attaching their curl output below.

jordan (Customer): getting this after you rotated certs? we started seeing timeouts right after 14:10Z. some requests succeed, most fail with handshake timeout. stack traces attached in case it helps.

maria (Support): thanks. can you paste curl and s_client logs? also which region and hostname?

jordan (Customer): region: us-west-2, host: api.redwood-inference.com, customer org: acme-marketing. curl:

```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer xxxxx\" 
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
*   Trying 34.216.12.45...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.com (34.216.12.45) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLS 1.3 connection timeout
* SSL connect error
* Failed to connect to api.redwood-inference.com port 443: Operation timed out
```

and openssl s_client:

```
$ openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com -tlsextdebug -status
CONNECTED(00000003)
1398471:error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:292
---
no peer certificate available
---
```

maria (Support): noted. @ajay can you check edge logs for TLS handshake failures around that time? this might be related to cert rotation that ran at 14:05Z (deploy-bot mentioned in builds).

ajay (SRE): looking. pulling edge-proxy logs for us-west-2 from 14:00-14:30Z. initial grep shows surge of TLS handshake_timeouts and connection resets. sample log lines: 

```
[2025-11-02T14:09:58Z] edge-proxy us-west-2 client_ip=34.216.12.45 method=POST path=/v1/generate tls_handshake_ms=12001 status=504 backend=none
[2025-11-02T14:10:02Z] edge-proxy us-west-2 client_ip=18.205.33.22 method=POST path=/v1/generate tls_error=handshake_timeout status=502
```

ajay (SRE): looks like the handshake attempt timed out after 12s repeatedly. backend didn't get the request. also seeing increased NXDOMAIN and SERVFAIL from our internal resolver cache around 14:08-14:12Z.

laura (NetworkOps): i pulled the dns-resolver metrics — we had a brief flapping on resolver-rack-3; error rate spiked when cert-rotator pod restarted and attempted to push new certs to the edge nodes. some nodes started rejecting due to an unexpected cipher mismatch with the new cert chain.

maria (Support): so two things: resolver instability and cert chain/cipher mismatch after rotation. any quick repro steps we can ask customer to run to validate?

ajay (SRE): ask them to run these steps:

1) curl with --retry and verbose to confirm handshake timeouts:
```
curl -v --retry 3 https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
```
2) openssl s_client for full cert chain:
```
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com -showcerts
```
3) dig to check resolver results and TTLs:
```
dig +short api.redwood-inference.com @8.8.8.8
```

maria (Support): sent steps to jordan. jordan, can you run and paste outputs? also can you try hitting our secondary region endpoint (api-us-east-2.redwood-inference.com) and confirm if failures persist? that helps isolate edge vs customer networking.

jordan (Customer): ran the openssl command — chain shows only one cert (the new leaf) and no intermediate. get the handshake error: 
```
verify return:1
depth=0 CN=api.redwood-inference.com
2508:error:0A000126:SSL routines:tls_process_server_certificate:certificate verify failed:../ssl/statem/statem_clnt.c:xxxx
```

curl to us-east-2 succeeded. us-east-2 returns full chain and healthy responses.

maria (Support): important: us-east-2 ok -> likely rotation pushed incomplete chain to us-west-2 edge nodes. @deploy-bot when did the cert rotation job run and which nodes were targeted?

deploy-bot: cert-rotator v2 started at 2025-11-02T14:05Z. rollout strategy: parallel per-rack, 30s drain between racks. 90% completion reported at 14:07:20Z. no rollback executed.

ajay (SRE): correlating timestamps — resolver flapping started ~14:08, cert-rotator reported 90% at 14:07. hypothesis: some edge nodes got partial chain; some had new cert, others old; clients/ALPN negotiation failed against mismatched chain/ciphers and resulted in handshake timeouts. Also resolver cache churn made some requests hit bad nodes.

laura (NetworkOps): immediate mitigation options:
- Roll back cert-rotator to previous cert bundle for us-west-2 racks with failures.
- Force re-provision full cert chain (leaf + intermediate) to all edge nodes (preferred).
- Temporarily route traffic away from failing racks to healthy racks/regions via smart-routing policy.

ajay (SRE): i recommend we provision full chain and roll forward rather than rollback; rollback risks other clients already trusting new cert. but we can re-deploy correct chain to nodes that have incomplete chain and remove affected nodes from rotation until they have full chain.

maria (Support): agreed. jordan — trying to repro here. for short-term workaround please point your requests to api-us-east-2 while we fix us-west-2. i'll request a short credit for downtime.

customer-acct-ops: issuing goodwill credit for 2 hours while SRE works through fix.

laura (NetworkOps): provisioning full chain now to all us-west-2 edge nodes. starting targeted push to rack-3 first. 14:34Z push initiated.

ajay (SRE): verifying after push — tailing edge logs, seeing decreased tls_error rates. sample: 
```
[2025-11-02T14:36:12Z] edge-proxy us-west-2 client_ip=54.210.45.11 method=POST path=/v1/generate tls_handshake_ms=85 status=200 backend=backend-12
```

maria (Support): jordan — can you re-test now?

jordan (Customer): re-tested. us-west-2 now returning 200. openssl shows full chain. huge improvement, thank you.

maria (Support): closing loop — root cause: cert-rotator v2 pushed incomplete chain to a subset of us-west-2 edge nodes while our internal resolver experienced a short flap; result was routing to mixed-state nodes causing TLS handshake timeouts and gateway 502/504s.

ajay (SRE): action items:
- create follow-up ticket to add preflight validation in cert-rotator: ensure full chain present on each node before marking success.
- add golden check to edge deployment that validates openssl s_client and full chain post-rotation.
- add alert on internal resolver SERVFAIL spike to auto-throttle rotation jobs.

laura (NetworkOps): i'll add a runbook to re-route traffic when resolver error rate > X% during sensitive rollout windows.

maria (Support): i've sent postmortem summary and remediation timeline to jordan and created support case link: CASE-2025-1102-0156. assigning to @ajay for follow-up.

ajay (SRE): got it. i'll file the cert-rotator preflight PR and link to the incident. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

inc-bot: incident CLOSED — severity: high — duration: 00:22:53 — postmortem pending

maria (Support): closing thread, will follow up with postmortem once ready.
